title: I Took the Rideshare Detour Screenshot to Safety

parts.text: I watched the little car on the map turn away from my street. I am twenty-two, late shift, phone at 12 percent. The driver, a man named Ed, said GPS was drunk. We were three extra minutes into a dark frontage road. The car smelled like cinnamon air freshener, too strong. I had already shared the trip with my sister Mara. Ed said, "Shortcut, relax" I said, "Pull over at the lit gas station" Ed's phone kept buzzing with a second app. I photographed the detour and the dash time, 1:14 a.m. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is still driving the frontage road, my battery is at 12 percent, and Mara is watching the pin.

social.description: Cinnamon overload, 12 percent battery, and a shortcut that was not on the route. Would you have named the gas station?

parts.text: He laughed, then saw I had the door handle and the app's safety button. He pulled into the 24-hour station with the humming coolers. I got out, ended the trip, and waited in the snack aisle under brutal light. Mara stayed on the phone. A clerk named Dina let me sit near the register. The app credited me and banned the route pattern after I sent screenshots. Ed one-starred me for being rude. I can live with rude. I cannot live with cinnamon and a frontage road. I take the extra two dollars for wait time now. My battery pack lives in my bag like a pet. Dina said, "You want water" I said, "Yes, and to stay until my sister's pin arrives" Dina said the coolers hum worse at 1 a.m. I still hear them when I close my eyes on purpose. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i.
